title: The promised land is not Judaea
source_text: Εἴπερ οὖν „ἡ“ πᾶσα „γῆ“ αὐτὴ „ἐπικατάρατος ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις“ ἐστὶ τοῦ Ἀδὰμ καὶ τῶν ἐν αὐτῷ ἀποθανόντων, δῆλον ὅτι καὶ πάντα τὰ μόρια αὐτῆς μετέχει τῆς ἀρᾶς. ἐν οἷς ἐστι καὶ ἡ Ἰουδαία γῆ· ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι ἐφαρμόζειν αὐτῇ τὸ „εἰς γῆν ἀγαθὴν καὶ πολλὴν. εἰς γῆν ῥέουσαν γάλα καὶ μέλι,“ κἂν συμβολικῶς σκιὰ εἶναι ἀποδεικνύηται ἡ Ἰουδαία καὶ ἡ Ἱερουσαλὴμ τῆς καθαρᾶς ἐν καθαρῷ κειμένης οὐρανῷ γῆς ἀγαθῆς καὶ πολλῆς, ἐν ᾗ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπουράνιος Ἱερουσαλήμ· περὶ ἧς διαλαβὼν ὁ ἀπόστολος, ὡς συνεγερθεὶς „Χριστῷ“ καὶ „τὰ ἄνω“ ζητῶν καὶ νοῦν εὑρὼν οὐδεμιᾶς ἐχόμενον Ἰουδαϊκῆς μυθολογίας φησίν· „ἀλλὰ προσεληλύθατε Σιὼν ὄρει καὶ πόλει θεοῦ ζῶντος Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ καὶ μυριάσιν ἀγγέλων πανηγύρει.“ ἵνα δέ τις πεισθῇ μὴ παρὰ τὸ βούλημα τοῦ θείου πνεύματος ἡμᾶς λέγειν περὶ τῆς παρὰ Μωϋσεῖ γῆς ἀγαθῆς καὶ πολλῆς, ἐπιστησάτω πᾶσι μὲν τοῖς προφήταις, διδάσκουσι τὴν εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπάνοδον τῶν πεπλανημένων καὶ ἀποπεπτωκότων ἀπ᾿ αὐτῆς καὶ ἁπαξαπλῶς ἀποκαθισταμένων εἰς τὸν καλούμενον τόπον καὶ πόλιν τοῦ θεοῦ παρὰ τῷ εἰπόντι ὅτι „ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἁγίᾳ ὁ τόπος αὐτοῦ,“ λέγοντι δὲ καὶ τό· „μέγας ὁ κύριος καὶ αἰνετὸς σφόδρα ἐν πόλει τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν, ὄρει ἁγίῳ αὐτοῦ, εὐρίζονι ἀγαλλιάματι πάσης τῆς γῆς.“ ἀρκεῖ δ᾿ ἐπὶ τοῦ παρόντος παραθέσθαι τὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ τριακοστοῦ καὶ ἕκτου ψαλμοῦ, οὕτως ἔχοντα περὶ τῆς τῶν δικαίων γῆς· „οἱ δ᾿ ὑπομένοντες (τὸν) κύριον αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσι γῆν“ καὶ μετ᾿ ὀλίγα· „οἱ δὲ πραεῖς κληρονομήσουσι γῆν καὶ κατατρυφήσουσιν ἐπὶ πλήθει εἰρήνης“ καὶ μετ᾿ ὀλίγα· „οἱ εὐλογοῦντες αὐτὸν κληρονομήσουσι γῆν“ καὶ πάλιν· „οἱ δίκαιοι κληρονομήσουσι γῆν καὶ κατασκηνώσουσιν εἰς αἰῶνα αἰῶνος ἐπ᾿ αὐτῆς.“ ὅρα δ᾿ εἰ μὴ τὸ καθαρὰν εἶναι ἐν καθαρῷ τῷ οὐρανῷ τὴν γῆν δηλοῦται τοῖς ἀκούειν δυναμένοις τῶν οὕτως εἰρημένων ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ ψαλμῷ· „ὑπόμεινον τὸν κύριον καὶ φύλαξον τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ. καὶ ὑψώσει σε τοῦ κατακληρονομῆσαι γῆν.“
pass_a_gloss: If then (εἴπερ οὖν) the whole earth (γῆ) itself is cursed (ἐπικατάρατος) in the works (ἔργα) of Adam and of those who died (ἀποθνῄσκω) in him, clear (δῆλον) that also all its parts (μόρια) partake (μετέχω) of the curse (ἀρά); among which is also the Judaean land (Ἰουδαία γῆ); so that the words ‘into a land good and large (ἀγαθὴ καὶ πολλή), into a land flowing (ῥέω) with milk and honey’ cannot fit (ἐφαρμόζω) it, even if Judaea and Jerusalem are shown symbolically (συμβολικῶς) to be a shadow (σκιά) of the good and large land, pure (καθαρά), lying (κεῖμαι) in a pure heaven (οὐρανός), in which is the heavenly (ἐπουράνιος) Jerusalem; about which the apostle, treating (διαλαμβάνω), as one raised together (συνεγείρω) with Christ and seeking the things above (τὰ ἄνω) and having found a sense (νοῦς) holding to (ἔχομαι) no Jewish mythology (μυθολογία), says: ‘But you have come to Mount Zion and the city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels, festal assembly (πανήγυρις).’ That someone be persuaded (πείθω) that we do not speak contrary to the intent (βούλημα) of the divine Spirit (πνεῦμα) about the good and large land in Moses, let him attend (ἐφίστημι) to all the prophets, teaching the return (ἐπάνοδος) to Jerusalem of those who wandered (πλανάω) and fell away (ἀποπίπτω) from it, and in a word (ἁπαξαπλῶς) of those restored (ἀποκαθίστημι) to the so-called place (τόπος) and city of God in (παρά + dat.) him who said ‘in holy peace (εἰρήνη) is his place’, and saying also ‘great the Lord and praised (αἰνετός) exceedingly in the city of our God, in his holy mountain, well-rooted (εὔριζος) with exultation (ἀγαλλίαμα) of all the earth’. Suffices for the present to set out (παρατίθημι) the words from the thirty-sixth psalm, thus about the land of the righteous (δίκαιοι): ‘but those who wait on (ὑπομένω) the Lord, they shall inherit (κληρονομέω) the land’; and after a little ‘the meek (πραεῖς) shall inherit land and delight (κατατρυφάω) in abundance of peace’; and after a little ‘those blessing (εὐλογέω) him shall inherit land’; and again ‘the righteous shall inherit land and encamp (κατασκηνόω) on it to age of age’. See whether the land being pure in the pure heaven is not shown (δηλόω) to those able to hear (ἀκούω + gen.) the words in the same psalm: ‘wait for the Lord and guard his way, and he will exalt (ὑψόω) you to inherit (κατακληρονομέω) land.’
pass_b_english: If, then, the whole “earth” is itself “cursed in the works” (Genesis 3:17) of Adam and of those who died in him (1 Corinthians 15:22), it is clear that all its parts share in the curse as well. Among them is the land of Judaea, so that the words “into a good and large land, into a land flowing with milk and honey” (Exodus 3:8) cannot be fitted to it. This holds even if Judaea and Jerusalem are shown to be, in a symbolic way, a shadow of the good and large land, pure and lying in a pure heaven, in which is the heavenly Jerusalem. Of this Jerusalem the apostle speaks as one who had been raised together with Christ and was seeking the things above (Colossians 3:1), and who had found a meaning bound to no Jewish fable. He says: “But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels in festal gathering” (Hebrews 12:22).

So that anyone may be persuaded that what we say about the good and large land in Moses is not contrary to the intention of the divine Spirit, let him give his attention to all the prophets. They teach the return to Jerusalem of those who have wandered and fallen away from it, and, in a word, of those who are being restored to what is called the place and city of God in the words of the one who said, “His place is in holy peace” (Psalm 76:2), and who also says, “Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, on his holy mountain, well rooted, with the joy of the whole earth” (Psalm 48:1–2).

But for the present it is enough to set out the words of the thirty-sixth Psalm (Psalm 37), which speak thus about the land of the righteous: “But those who wait for the Lord, they shall inherit the land” (Psalm 37:9); and a little after, “But the meek shall inherit the land and delight in abundance of peace” (Psalm 37:11); and a little after, “Those who bless him shall inherit the land” (Psalm 37:22); and again, “The righteous shall inherit the land and dwell upon it for ever and ever” (Psalm 37:29). And see whether, to those who are able to hear these words in the same Psalm, it is not made plain that the earth is pure in the pure heaven: “Wait for the Lord and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land” (Psalm 37:34).

choices.choice: γῆ is rendered ‘earth’ where Origen speaks of the cursed earth and of Plato’s pure earth, and ‘land’ in the promise texts; Origen’s argument is that these are one and the same γῆ, so a reader should hear the same word in both. LXX numbering converted: Psalm 75:3 LXX = Psalm 76:2 English (LXX ‘his place was made in peace’; Origen’s text adds ‘holy’); Psalm 47:2–3 LXX = Psalm 48:1–2 English; ‘thirty-sixth Psalm’ (Origen’s LXX number) kept in the text with the English number Psalm 37 in parentheses; verses 37:9, 11, 22, 29, 34 checked by wording. Psalm 37:22 follows the LXX ‘those who bless him’ (Hebrew: those blessed by him). ‘Those who died in him’ is an uncited-by-Origen echo of 1 Corinthians 15:22 (‘in Adam all die’), cited as a clear allusion. Origen ascribes Hebrews to ‘the apostle’; kept. ‘Pure, lying in a pure heaven’ echoes Plato, Phaedo 109b, quoted by Celsus in the previous chapter. ‘Jewish fable’ may echo Titus 1:14 (‘Jewish myths’); possible allusion, not cited inline. παρὰ τῷ εἰπόντι means ‘in the writer who said’ (the psalmist), not the agent of the restoring. In the last sentence τῶν οὕτως εἰρημένων is taken with ἀκούειν (‘able to hear these words’). Koetschau’s (τὸν) in Psalm 37:9 is an editorial supplement and does not change the sense.
‘restored to ... the place and city of God by the one who said’ read as if the psalmist did the restoring; παρὰ τῷ εἰπόντι fixed to ‘in the words of the one who said’
Psalm 48:2 εὐρίζονι ἀγαλλιάματι: ‘well rooted, the joy of the whole earth’ to ‘well rooted, with the joy of the whole earth’ (dative, not apposition)
Marked the μέν/δέ turn with ‘But for the present’ and kept the δέ of Psalm 37:9 (‘But those who wait’)
Last sentence reworded: τῶν οὕτως εἰρημένων taken with ἀκούειν; stiff ‘the earth’s being pure’ replaced by ‘that the earth is pure in the pure heaven’
All twelve citations checked against LXX wording; LXX Psalm numbers converted correctly

Two style calls were made without that check: (1) 'his Son' is capitalised in Celsus's speech (7.18) to match 'the Father' there, but the sibling chunks of other books are mixed (29 'his son' against 24 'his Son'), so a corpus-wide pass may be wanted; (2) Origen's LXX ordinal 'hundred and thirty-sixth psalm' (7.22, 7.29) is kept in the text, with the English citation (Psalm 137:8–9) beside it.
